sections.heading: For the home you live in
paragraphs: MEL ONE provides handyman repairs and household maintenance in Adelaide. Our team arranges an on-site assessment, identifies the work required and confirms the repair plan and written quote. The starting point is everyday life at home: a cupboard that no longer closes neatly, furniture waiting to be assembled, a worn screen or a garden that needs attention.
Single repairs and longer lists both start with your description and Adelaide suburb. Tell MEL ONE what needs attention and the outcome you would like; our team checks the work on site.

sections.heading: Start with what you can see
paragraphs: Describe the job, where it is and how it affects the use of your home. Add your suburb and preferred timing. Photos are optional; email safe existing images to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au. For assembly, a product name and available instructions help us prepare.

We confirm access and the assessment appointment, check the affected item or measure for new work, and explain the materials, proposed work and written quote. Any further assessment or additional work is agreed with you before proceeding. You do not need to diagnose a fault to make contact.

sections.heading: Bring the whole household list
paragraphs: Several small jobs can be easier to describe together. Group your list by room or outdoor area, add a short note beside each item and point out anything that affects daily use. A loose handle, a wall patch and a flat-pack shelf can all go in the same enquiry.
MEL ONE checks each listed task on site and confirms which work can be combined, the materials, access, timing and quote. Identify the owner or manager who can approve the work.

sections.heading: A clear place for specialist work
paragraphs: Contact MEL ONE with your Adelaide suburb and job details. Our team arranges an on-site assessment, checks the reported concern or new-work requirements and confirms the scope, quote and appointment. Safe existing photos are optional; email them to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au.
Where licensed work or formal project approvals are part of the job, MEL ONE confirms the qualified service arrangements, work scope and required documents before work begins.

paragraphs: Call 0416 614 281 or email admin@melonemaintenance.com.au with a short description of your household-maintenance request and your Adelaide suburb. Include your preferred reply method so we can arrange the assessment appointment, check the work on site and confirm the scope and quote.
The contact address is 63 Pirie St Adelaide SA 5000. Contact MEL ONE to arrange your site visit or discuss visiting the office.

method.title: How it works
method.description: Tell MEL ONE what needs attention and your Adelaide suburb. We confirm the appointment, assess the job on site and explain the work plan and written quote. These eight steps cover preparation, qualified service arrangements, your approval and the completion record.

steps.heading: Describe the job; photos are optional
paragraphs: Start with what you can see: what needs attention, where it is and how it affects everyday use. Add your Adelaide suburb or postcode and the outcome you would like. MEL ONE arranges the assessment, checks the affected area and confirms the repair approach and written quote.

Photos are optional: email safe existing images to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au. A wider view can show the location and a close view the detail, but a description is enough to request assessment. Keep personal paperwork out of frame and leave heavy items, covers and damaged fittings in place. For assembly, include the product name and instructions if available.

steps.heading: Put the household list in one place
paragraphs: If you have several jobs, group them by room or outdoor area. Give each item a short description and mark the ones that most affect daily use. A loose cupboard handle, an unfinished shelf and a worn screen can be described in the same enquiry.

Explain whether the jobs depend on one another or on a delivery, another person or access to the property. A grouped list helps frame the discussion; whether any tasks can be combined depends on their individual scope, site conditions and the availability confirmed for the request.

steps.heading: Talk through the details
paragraphs: Call 0416 614 281 or email admin@melonemaintenance.com.au with your description and preferred reply method. We confirm the assessment appointment and access, then check the reported work on site. We explain the materials, work plan, written quote and timing before you approve the work. Photos are optional; email safe existing images to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au. Identify who can approve work if an owner or property manager is involved.

For installation or assembly, MEL ONE checks measurements, existing fittings and any product information during the assessment. For repairs, we inspect the concern and investigate the cause before proposing the scope. Keep a note of the information still needed and the next action agreed. We confirm the assessment appointment, inspect the affected area or measure for new work, and explain the proposed scope and written quote. You approve the agreed work before it begins.

steps.heading: Identify what needs specialist assessment
paragraphs: MEL ONE arranges an on-site assessment for electrical, structural and approval-dependent requests. Describe the visible concern from a safe accessible position and leave fittings in their current condition. We confirm appropriately qualified service arrangements, the proposed work and required project documents before work begins.

MEL ONE checks which tasks form part of the household-maintenance scope and which require licensed work, inspection or approval. We discuss the service arrangements and confirm the agreed work with you before scheduling.

steps.heading: Agree the details before scheduling
paragraphs: MEL ONE confirms the assessment or repair appointment with you, including the visit purpose, authorised contact and access arrangements. We explain the scope, materials and quote before agreed repair work begins.

Keep the agreed details together so everyone is referring to the same list. If the list changes, raise it before assuming the additional item is included. Confirm the purpose of any proposed visit, especially when it is to assess a concern rather than carry out an agreed repair.

steps.heading: Prepare the space for an agreed visit
paragraphs: Once a visit is confirmed, discuss entry, parking or shared-access restrictions and who will be present. Keep product instructions, agreed parts and the job list accessible. Move small personal items only where it is safe to do so; describe furniture or other obstacles that need separate handling.

Plan how children and pets will stay away from the work area, and mention any limits on room access or use. Share necessary entry details directly through the agreed contact method. Prepare from ground level and leave fittings and heavy items in place for the agreed visit.

steps.heading: Keep the work tied to the agreed scope
paragraphs: For an agreed work visit, use the original list to identify the location and intended outcome of each task. Discuss any relevant site conditions before a work method is settled. Photos and descriptions may not reveal concealed conditions, the suitability of a surface or the condition of an existing fitting.

If conditions suggest a change, ask what needs to be agreed before additional work proceeds, including any effect on materials, timing or the quote. An item needing further assessment may remain outside the agreed work. Keep access questions and any changes connected to the same household list.

steps.heading: Review the result and the next steps
paragraphs: At the end of an agreed work visit, refer back to the job list and discuss which items were addressed and which remain outstanding. Ask about any relevant care instructions, materials information and agreed handling of leftover items or waste. Raise questions about the work while the details are clear.

Keep a record of any remaining assessment, separate work or information needed and who is taking the next step. If you notice a concern afterwards, contact MEL ONE with the job details and safe photos where useful. Any further work, timing and scope need their own confirmation.

sections.heading: Describe what happens in normal use
paragraphs: Name the item and its exact location, such as an internal bedroom door, patio screen or window in a particular room. Describe what you observe: catching, looseness, torn mesh or a handle that does not operate normally, while focusing on the visible condition.

Everyday impact is useful context. Note whether access is awkward, a room cannot be used as expected or the issue appears only when opening in one direction. Leave the item and its hardware in their current condition, then share a safe description or photo.

sections.heading: Collect a clear, safe record
paragraphs: Optional photos can show the item’s location and visible concern. Email safely taken existing images to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au if available; a description is enough. Leave the item and hardware in their current condition.

Include an approximate age if known and an existing product label only when it is easily visible. If glass is broken, a door is coming away from its track or a frame is unstable, stop using it and keep people clear. Leave the assembly in place and contact MEL ONE with the visible condition.

sections.heading: Arrange assessment and agree the repair
paragraphs: Send the location, observed issue, desired outcome, Adelaide suburb and preferred reply method in one message. If a tenant, owner or property manager is involved, identify who can discuss access and who can approve proposed work.

MEL ONE reviews the information, confirms assessment and access arrangements, and explains the proposed repair scope and price basis before work is booked. Identify who can approve the work so the next step is clear.

sections.heading: Sliding screen door: find the part that needs attention
paragraphs: MEL ONE checks the mesh, rollers and guides, track and frame together before recommending a repair. A torn screen and a door that drags are different problems; replacing one part without checking the assembly can leave the original fault unresolved.
items: Mesh: a tear or loose edge with an otherwise sound frame points to a mesh repair discussion. We check the frame, fixing detail and required mesh before agreeing the work.
Rollers and guides: dragging, uneven movement or a door sitting out of alignment prompts a check of rollers, guides and their adjustment, alongside track and frame condition.
Track: accumulated debris, a damaged running surface or distortion requires a track check. We confirm whether cleaning, adjustment, local repair or a broader replacement scope addresses the problem.

Frame: bent, loose or damaged sections affect how the mesh and hardware work together. We compare a defined frame repair with replacement when a reliable repair needs more than a new roller or fresh mesh.

sections.heading: Match replacement parts before agreeing the scope
paragraphs: Rollers, guides, mesh and frame fittings are not interchangeable across every door. MEL ONE checks the existing assembly, accessible product markings and component fit before confirming replacement parts. Photos help us prepare, while the assessment confirms the details needed for the work.

The quote should identify which components are included, the number of screens or doors, inspection and access arrangements, parts sourcing and any frame or track work. We explain any additional findings before expanding the agreed scope.

sections.heading: Keep insect screens and security screens distinct
paragraphs: An ordinary insect screen is intended to keep insects out; it is not evidence of a security screen rating. Tell MEL ONE whether the item is an insect screen or a security screen and share visible product markings if available. Security fittings and any claimed certification are checked as part of the scope; replacing mesh or rollers does not establish a security rating.

Do not remove the door, test an unstable frame or handle broken glass to obtain photos. A written description is enough to request assessment. Safe existing photos are optional; email them to admin@melonemaintenance.com.au.

faqs.question: Can torn mesh be repaired without replacing the whole screen door?
faqs.answer: Yes, a mesh-only scope is useful when the existing frame and fittings are sound. MEL ONE checks those parts first, then confirms the mesh and work included.

faqs.question: Will new rollers always fix a dragging door?
faqs.answer: No. We check rollers and guides together with the track, alignment and frame. The repair scope addresses the parts causing the poor movement.

faqs.question: Can photos confirm the replacement parts and final price?
faqs.answer: Photos help identify the assembly and prepare the assessment. MEL ONE confirms component matching, site condition and the agreed pricing basis before work is booked.

faqs.question: When should I compare repair with replacement?
faqs.answer: Compare the options when the frame or track is damaged, matching parts are unavailable or several components require work. MEL ONE explains the repair scope and replacement option against the condition of your assembly.
